newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bank PDFCI active on report of stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Bank PDFCI active on report of stake sale.

text.p: Shares of Bank Private Development Finance Company of Indonesia (PDFCI) were active in late morning trade on Monday following reports that Bank Indonesia plans to sell its stake in the bank, brokers said.
The share was up 425 rupiah to 3,225 at 0440 GMT.
Bisnis Indonesia newspaper quoted central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono as saying Bank Indonesia planned to sell its stake in Bank PDFCI, Bank Papan Sejahtera and Bank Ficorinvest.

The governor was quoted as saying during a speech in Hong Kong that the central bank will sell all its stakes in commercial banks to avoid a conflict of interest. But he did not give a time-frame for the move.
"The reports created some speculation of possible buyers in the market," a broker with a Japanese securities firm said.
He added that some leading business figures, including President Suharto's daughter Siti Hediati Prabowo, had been rumoured as prospective buyers in Bank PDFCI.
Another broker said she heard that conglomerate Lippo Group could be interested in purchasing a stake in PDFCI.
"As far as I know, no prospective buyers have conducted any discussion with Bank Indonesia about purchasing a stake in our bank," Sukamto, Bank PDFCI managing director told Reuters.
He also said that there was a consensus among the founders that if one shareholder planned to sell its stake, other shareholders would have the right of first refusal.
